text:
Maria: ran a small queueing sim this morning to compare microbatch granularity vs waiting for headroom. attaching key output below, tl;dr: smaller microbatches reduce p99 tail but cut throughput ~12% at 90% util.
Sam: can you paste the sim command you used?
Maria: sure: `./tools/queue-sim --trace traces/weekday_peak.json --microbatch-sizes 1,4,8,16 --safety-factor 0.8 --kv-warmup true`
Maria: sample output:
```
Config: microbatch=4 safety=0.8 kv_warmup=enabled
GPU_util_target=0.9
Throughput: 980 req/s (mb=4)
p95=42ms p99=120ms
mb=8 -> 1120 req/s p95=55ms p99=210ms
mb=1 -> 860 req/s p95=38ms p99=95ms
KV_miss_rate=0.06
```
Ben: interesting — mb=8 hits higher aggregate throughput but p99 doubles. that's the headroom vs saturation tradeoff we worried about.
Olga: whats the safety-factor doing in the sim? is it admission threshold (0-1) before we accept a request into a batch?
Maria: yes, safety-factor scales the estimated in-flight load we allow. lower safety -> more aggressive admission, higher util.
Ava: do you model KV cache cold-start costs? that looks like kv_miss rate driving tail for larger microbatches.
Maria: kv warmup toggle uses sampled prefix caching; when off, p99 for mb=8 goes to 320ms. so bigger batches amplify kvmiss slowpath.
Sam: could be the kernel choice on the slowpath too — larger batches force an attention kernel that has worse small-seq latency. any kernel-switch events logged?
Maria: yes, saw kernel flip to attn_v2_slow at high batch sizes. correlates with the p99 spike.
Ben: that smells like a perf regression from the tuning that prioritized throughput. we need a guard: don't switch to slow kernel when we predict >x% tail contribution.
Olga: propose adding a fastpath-only admission policy for latency-SLO routes. accept only microbatch<=4 or drop to higher-cost perp-token kernel but with admission fallback.
Ava: or add a staged queuing window: wait up to 8ms to fill a microbatch, otherwise serve smaller batch. yields better p95 and acceptable throughput loss.
Sam: agree. also add a metric for "kernel-switch-rate" and "slowpath-latency" so we can alert before SLOs break.
CI-bot: perf-test (edge) pipeline triggered: perf/queue-sim/1991239999 -> running
Maria: next steps I'm proposing: 1) run kernel-level flamegraph on mb=8 slowpath, 2) simulate staged-wait window 6-10ms, 3) add kernel-switch alert and slowpath drop counter, 4) run a canary with safety-factor=0.7 on a dedicated pool.
Ben: for the canary, gate rollout by p99 delta<20% and GPU util delta<5%. if fail, auto-roll back.
Olga: also check KV prefetch heuristics — maybe prefetch TTL and eviction policy interaction is causing spikes. small batches warm better but bigger batches thrash the cache.
Ava: one more: record per-request kv_latency histogram (not just global) so we can correlate kvmiss tail against request size and prompt length.
Sam: I can add the kernel-switch metric today. Maria, can you share the sim config in the ticket?
Maria: uploaded config + raw traces to GH issue #4782. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4782
Olga: cool. putting a quick note on the runbook: if p99 increases >1.5x and kernel-switch-rate >0.05, enable slowpath-shed policy (drop low-priority requests) and flip to conservative kernels.
Ben: :thumbsup: let's keep the conservative default for public SLO routes until we validate prefetch fixes.
Maria: thanks team — will post perf flamegraph and canary results later today.
